IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL 
Criminal Writ Petition No. 517 of 2008
With 
Stay Application No. 4186/2008
Meharban S/o Asgar R/o Vill. Bhugganpur, 
P.S. Kotwali Manglaur, District Hardwar
............. Petitioner. 
Versus 
1. State of Uttarakhand through S.S.P. Hardwar
2. S.O. Pathri, Distt. Hardwar
………… Respondents 
Sri Manish Arora, learned counsel for the petitioner
Sri M.A. Khan, learned brief holder for the State. 
Coram: Hon’ble Prafulla C. Pant, J. 
 Hon’ble Dharam Veer, J. 
Dated: July 10, 2008
Heard Sri Manish Arora, learned counsel for the
petitioner and Sri M.A. Khan, learned brief holder for the
State. 
By means of this writ petition, the petitioner has sought
quashing of the first information report dated 18.6.2008
registered as Case Crime No. 79/2008 relating to offence
punishable under Section2/3 of U.P. Gangsters & Anti Social
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986 with P.S. Pathri, Distt.
Hardwar. 
Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that there is a
single case shown against the petitioner in the gang chart and
that is not sufficient to show “activities” required for the
purposes of constituting the offence punishable u/s 2/3 of
U.P. Gangsters & Anti Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986.
However, having gone through the contents of the FIR and the
seriousness of the allegations, we are not inclined to interfere
in the present matter. 
Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed summarily. (Stay
Application No. 4186/08 also stands dismissed) 
(Dharam Veer, J.) (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
10.07.2008
Rajeev Dang

WPSS No.517 of 2008 
Hon’ble Tarun Agarwala, J.
Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, the learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. N. S. Pundir, the learned brief holder for the State of 
Uttarakhand. 
An advertisement was published for filling up of 134 posts 
of Sub-Inspector and Platoon Commanders in Civil Police as well 
as in Provincial Armed Costabulary (P.A.C.). Pursuant to this, 
the petitioner applied and appeared in the written examination. 
Results were declared on 10th January, 2007 in which the name of 
the petitioner was not found and, being aggrieved, the present 
writ petition was filed. 
The counter affidavit indicates that the petitioner had 
applied under the O.B.C. category and the cut off marks for the 
O.B.C. candidates was 185, whereas the petitioner has obtained 
only 130.75 marks. This fact has not been denied by the 
petitioner since no rejoinder affidavit has been filed inspite of 
filing counter affidavit in August, 2008. 
In the light of the aforesaid, the court does not find any 
reason to interfere in the impugned order. The writ petition fails 
and is dismissed. 
 (Tarun Agarwala, J.) 
Dated 19.06.2012
